then.text: Rain's good for paint, you know. Washes the salt off and leaves the colours bright as a box of sweeties.
Look at that harbour in the sun. Every colour I've ever painted, all lined up and showing off.
At dusk the houses go soft, like someone's turned the colours down a notch. Still my favourite time.

house_painter.text: {greeting} Every house on the quay is a different colour. They say it was so fishermen could find their own front door from the sea. In the dark. With a dram.
Reds, yellows, blues. I keep a tin of each. When one house fades, the neighbour's the same shade by sunset. I'm retired. The paint is not.

then.text: Raining, and the bus is late. Two things you can always count on here. Three, if you count me.
In this fog the bus could be right in front of me and I'd not know. I'll wave at every noise, just in case.
Still waiting, and the sun's going down. I've decided I'm not late, I'm just very early for tomorrow.

bus_waiter.text: {greeting} The 57 to Uig is due at ten past. I've been here since twenty to. It's ten past, and the bus is, as ever, in a different time zone.
I'm a patient person. It's the only way to live on an island. The ferry's late, the bus is late, and the weather's pretty much right on time.

then.text: A gale on the Minch! If the Blue Men show up, I'll rhyme till I'm hoarse. 'Gale' and 'sail'. 'Boat' and 'float'.
Thick fog on the water. Perfect weather for Blue Men, my granda would say. I've my rhymes ready.
Quiet night on the harbour. If you hear poetry out on the water, answer it. Just in case.

minch_sailor.text: The Blue Men of the Minch. They'd come up beside the boat in a storm and call out a line of poetry. You answered in rhyme, or the sea took your boat.
My granda made me learn forty rhymes. 'Weather' and 'together'. 'Fish' and 'dish'. A sailor never knows. I haven't met one yet. I'm ready, though.

then.text: In Gaelic, water is 'uisge'. On Skye that covers the sea, the lochs and most of the sky as well.
Madainn mhath! That's 'good morning', and I mean it. The sun's coming up over the Storr, look.

gaelic_teacher.text: Gaelic's spoken here every day, on Skye. I'm learning. 'Madainn mhath' is 'good morning', 'tapadh leibh' is 'thank you', and 'slàinte mhath' is 'good health'. I can say all three while sneezing.
Skye has a Gaelic college, Sabhal Mòr Ostaig, down in Sleat. People come from all over to learn. They say the grammar is easy. It is not.

por_creel.text: Langoustines in the creels, rain on my back, and a flask of tea. Don't pity me, this is the good life.

then.text: The Sound of Raasay's grey today. Bonny, mind you. Everything's bonny when you're back on dry land.

else.text: Painted houses so the boats can find home in the fog. Practical, and pretty.

por_harbourhand.text: That's Raasay out there, and the Cuillin behind it. Show-offs, the pair of them.
Ferry's on time, the weather's behaving, and somebody's put the kettle on. Good day to be a deckhand.

por_shopper.text: I came for a loaf and a postcard and I've been in three gift shops. Wool socks for everyone, at this rate.
Wind's up but I'm not. Wrap the scarf twice and carry on.

por_birder.text: Sea eagle over the bay this morning. I nearly dropped the flask. Nearly.

then.text: Can't see a thing, but you can hear them. Oystercatchers, I think. Possibly a very cross gull.

else.text: Binoculars, notebook, bacon roll. A birder's holy trinity.

por_ferryhand.text: The Harris boat. Across the Little Minch to Tarbert, on the Isle of Harris, in the Outer Hebrides. Fàilte, if you're going: that's welcome. Gaelic first, English second, sheep before either.

then.text: Edinburgh next. The traders' desk and the auction. You can't buy a hill without knowing what a hill costs.

else.text: The session book. Good. The Napier Commission, appointed in 1883, held its very first sitting at the Braes, and took evidence from crofters in their own words, a startling idea for the time.

Before that, in Sutherland, the Clearances emptied whole straths for sheep. People were moved to the coast or put on ships. It was not weather, and it was not fate; it was rent. Some places are green now where the houses stood, and anyone who knows why will not walk across them lightly.
A buyout needs a business plan or the bank laughs. Go to the Traders' desk at the Edinburgh Exchange and become a member, then ask about the auction rooms.
If Calum sent you, the kirk book is in the church. Look for the page with the pencil.

then.text: Fiona says you're a good egg. High praise, from Fiona.
You know Fiona already? Marvellous. She's doing the baking for the count and she says you're welcome in her kitchen. That counts as a reference, in the Highlands.

else.text: The ballot needs a catered night, and Fiona does the baking. She has a stall about the island and a face like a customs officer. Introduce yourself to her first; she'll know you when you do.
I'm organising the count night. Not until you've the proof, though. The proof is first.

arts_librarian.text: {greeting} Madainn mhath. The Gaelic shelf is the one nearest the window; the light is better and so is the poetry.

Sorley MacLean was born across the water on Raasay. His 'Hallaig' is about a village the landlord cleared in the 1850s, and in the poem the people come back as birch trees. Read it, then take the ferry and stand in the wood. Nobody comes back unchanged.

Màiri Mhòr nan Òran is the other one. Big Mary of the Songs. She could not write, so she sang them, and she sang them at the land meetings until the crofters got their Act in 1886. We keep her near the door so she can keep an eye on things.

then.text: The field's quiet. The Keeper's charm isn't. You can hear it from the road. Crex, crex, crex.

else.text: Not a peep from the bottom field. I haven't slept so well in years. I'd feel guilty, if I weren't so well rested.

then.text: We cut from the middle now, and slowly. It adds a day to the hay and takes a year off my temper. The chicks get away.

else.text: Four chicks in the iris by the end of July. The calling goes on all night, and I've learned to love it. I hope the neighbours have, too.
